extracted.intended_audience: OPQA reviewers / USPTO patent quality reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing USPTO office actions for omitted statutory rejections and documenting complete proposed rejections, evidence, and procedural characteristics for OPQA review. The form covers numerous statutory bases (35 USC 101, 103, 112 variants, double patenting) and office-action characteristics (allowability, rejoinder, reasons for allowance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough description of the omitted rejection(s) (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposed rejection for each of the claim(s) listed must be provided.  For each claim the statute, sub paragraph and evidence supporting the rejection must be clearly identified.  The proposed rejection should not be personalized, and should reflect a thorough analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete proposed rejection for each listed claim, identify the statute and the evidence supporting the rejection, avoid personalization, and analyze how the prior art or disclosure supports the legal conclusion (anticipation, obviousness, lack of enablement/written description, indefiniteness, ineligibility, lack of utility, double patenting, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: 35 U.S.C. 103 (Obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 when the invention is obvious subject matter. To support the conclusion that the claimed invention should have been rejected as directed to obvious subject matter, the proposed rejection should articulate a prima facie case of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of fact must be supported by sufficient evidence in the prior art. The rejection must articulate how the prior art is to be modified to arrive at the claimed invention. The reasoning/rationale should be taught by the prior art applied or provided by the reviewer in a convincing line of reasoning as to why the artisan would have found the claimed invention obvious in light of the applied prior art. Also: list each claim for which an omitted 103 rejection is proposed; do not list claims that already have a compliant rejection even if covered by the omitted combination (see provided example). Indicate whether omitted rejection applies to independent claims, dependent claims, or both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Reference(s) relied on in an omitted rejection (general reference data requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete for each reference applied in an omitted rejection: Name, Document Identifier, US(First) CPC Classification Symbol (if US patent doc), 'Found by', and Reference Type. For NPL docs, fill Document Identifier with bibliographic info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference is of record in an 892 or 1449, select 892/1449 for 'Found by' even if reviewer located it. If reference is a US patent document, provide Document Identifier and US(F) CPC symbol (use Classification Allocation Tool/CAT Tool). For NPL or other types without a US(F) CPC symbol, that column may be left blank. See MPEP 707.05(e) for guidance on citing NPLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how reviewer-located references were found (search-logic requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference was found by Reviewer Search or Other (and is not of record), provide the search string(s) or a detailed explanation of how and where the reference was located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all search logic, including all search strings and an indication of where the reference was ultimately found (e.g., specific search string or classification search). If found by other means, explain (e.g., ISA document, Background of the Invention, parent application). If a reference was ultimately of record, choose the appropriate 'Found by' code (892/1449) and note reviewer search in the Search/Prior Art section.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) Enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) Enablement if the disclosure, when filed, does not contain sufficient information regarding the subject matter of the claims as to enable one skilled in the pertinent art to make and use the claimed invention without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim for which an omitted 112(a) Enablement rejection is proposed (including dependent claims that inherit deficiencies). Indicate whether omission applies to independent claims, dependent claims, or both. Check applicable boxes for specifics (112(a) related to 112(f); insufficient reference to deposit of biological material; dependent claims inheriting deficiencies). Provide a complete proposed rejection for each listed claim, identify statute and evidence, avoid personalization, and analyze why the disclosure fails to enable without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) Written Description
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) Written Description if there is not sufficient written description to inform a skilled artisan that the applicant was in possession of the claimed invention as a whole at the time the application was filed. For newly added or amended claims, applicant should show support in the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim for which an omitted written-description rejection is proposed (including dependent claims inheriting deficiencies). Indicate whether omission applies to independent claims, dependent claims, or both. Check basis boxes (new matter; original claims; 112(a) related to 112(f); lack of sufficient algorithm for computer-implemented inventions; insufficient deposit reference for biological material; dependent claims inheriting deficiencies; or none). Provide a complete proposed rejection identifying statute and supporting evidence, explaining why the disclosure does not show possession of the claimed invention as a whole at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (Indefiniteness / Particularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) when the claims do not particularly point out and distinctly claim that which the inventor regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim proposed for an omitted 112(b) rejection (including dependent claims inheriting deficiencies). Indicate whether omission applies to independent claims, dependent claims, or both. Check all applicable bases from: relative terminology; ranges and amounts limitations; exemplary language (e.g., 'for example'); lack of antecedent basis; alternative limitations (e.g., Markush); unclaimed/omitted essential subject matter; relation to 112(f); unbounded functional claiming; dependent claims inheriting deficiencies; or 'Other'. Provide a complete proposed rejection per claim, identifying statute and evidence, and analyze how claims fail to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: 35 U.S.C. 112(d) (Improper Dependent Claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(d) as being directed to an improper dependent claim when the claim contains a reference to a previous claim and does not specify a further limitation and include all limitations of the previous claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim for which an omitted 112(d) rejection is proposed (including dependent claims inheriting deficiencies). Provide a complete proposed rejection for each listed claim, identify statute and evidence, and analyze how dependent claims fail to specify a further limitation and include all limitations of the referenced claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: 35 U.S.C. 101 Subject Matter Eligibility (SME)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 if it is not directed to one of the four statutory categories (process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter) or if the claim is directed to a judicial exception and the claim as a whole does not include additional limitations amounting to significantly more than the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim for which an omitted 101 SME rejection is proposed and indicate whether omission applies to independent/dependent/both. For Step 1 failures, check applicable categories (Transitory Signal/Signal per se; Program/Software per se; Human Organism; Use Claim; Information/data per se; Other). For Step 2, follow structured checks: 2(b)(1) identify judicial exception (product of nature, law of nature, natural phenomenon, abstract idea). If abstract idea, select subcategory (mathematical concept; certain methods of organizing human activity; mental process; tentative abstract idea per 2019 guidance). 2(b)(2) evaluate integration into a practical application (no additional elements; merely 'apply it'; adds insignificant extra-solution activity; merely links to a technological environment; or Other with explanation). 2(b)(3) evaluate inventive concept (no additional elements; merely 'apply it'; adds insignificant extra-solution; links to environment; appends well-understood routine/conventional activities — if last, support per Berkheimer options: Applicant statement, court decision, publication, or official notice). Provide a thorough proposed rejection for each claim, identify statute and evidence, and analyze why claims are not patent eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: 35 U.S.C. 101 Utility
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 Utility when there is no assertion of a specific and substantial credible utility by the applicant, and the claimed invention does not have readily apparent well-established utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim for which an omitted 101 Utility rejection is proposed (identify independent/dependent/both). Provide a complete proposed rejection for each claim, identify statute and supporting evidence, and analyze how the claims lack a specific and substantial credible utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: 35 U.S.C. Statutory Double Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under Statutory Double Patenting when the claimed invention is directed to the same invention (identical subject matter) claimed in a patent or co-pending application with at least one common inventor/assignee/applicant or under a Joint Research Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim for which an omitted statutory double-patenting rejection is proposed (identify independent/dependent/both). Must check basis (Provisional or Non-provisional). Identify conflicting patent/application relied on: complete columns including Name, Document Identifier, US(F) CPC Classification Symbol, Found by (Reviewer Search, 892, 1449, ISA, Other) and Reference Type. Ensure US patent/application numbers formatted correctly. Answer whether the omitted rejection is based on a rejection previously made during prosecution and improperly withdrawn in response to filing of a Terminal Disclaimer (Yes/No). Provide a complete proposed rejection per claim with statute and evidence, analyzing identical subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: MRF Omitted Rejection: Nonstatutory Double Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention should have been rejected under Nonstatutory Double Patenting when the claimed invention is not patentably distinct from an invention claimed in a patent or co-pending application with at least one common inventor/assignee/applicant or under a Joint Research Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim for which an omitted nonstatutory double-patenting rejection is proposed (identify independent/dependent/both). Indicate basis (Provisional or Non-provisional) and type of omitted rejection (Anticipatory Type and/or Obviousness Type). Identify conflicting patents/applications and any modifying references; specify for each whether it is the conflicting patent/application or a modifying reference, provide Name, Document Identifier, US(F) CPC symbol if applicable, Found by, Reference Type, and provide search explanation if found by Reviewer Search or Other. Indicate whether omission is based on a rejection dropped during prosecution because of a terminal disclaimer not accepted by the Office (Yes/No). Provide a complete proposed rejection and analysis of lack of patentable distinctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Action Characteristics: Clarification of 'Immediate Prosecution'
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise indicated, characteristics listed should be captured with respect to only the instant office action under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing characteristics (e.g., Allowable Subject Matter) capture them only for the instant office action unless notes indicate otherwise or the question language expressly broadens scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Action Characteristics: Allowable Subject Matter (questions & best practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the examiner indicated allowable subject matter and related prosecution characteristics: Did the examiner indicate allowable subject matter? Was rejoinder properly practiced? Is a reason for allowance present? Optional comments; check best-practice characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Q1: Answer 'Yes' only when examiner affirmatively allows a claim or indicates a claim as containing allowable subject matter (including allowances). 'No' if examiner simply does not reject/does not address claim. Q2: Rejoinder: answer Yes/No/N/A — apply MPEP 821.04 and appropriate form paragraphs; if 'No' provide details. Q3: Is there a reason for allowance (an explanation for how claims distinguish over prior art)? If Yes, indicate whether reasons add substance to the record. Q4: Optional comments/suggestions/best practices. Q5: Check all applicable best-practice boxes — presence of characteristics (does not require accolade-worthiness): (a) Office action identifies specific allowable subject matter and demonstrates how prior art neither anticipates nor renders obvious that allowable subject matter; (b) Check only when specific allowable subject matter is identified and there is an explanation as to how prior art does not anticipate/render obvious; (c) An Examiner’s Amendment was completed to place the case in condition for allowance; (d) Office action cites pertinent applicant arguments persuasive in overcoming a previous rejection; (e) Office action cites newly discovered prior art providing a brief description why it was cited but not applied; (f) Reasons for Allowance addresses each independent claim separately; (g) None of the above. Q6: Is there an accolade related to Allowable Subject Matter? — Only available if at least one of the above best-practices boxes is checked; follow current accolade procedures and guidance; when indicating an accolade, complete the specified sentence per procedures.
